title: Approve a safe, effective and reversible hormonal male contraceptive

concept.text: Prevent pregnancy through reversible hormonal suppression of sperm production while maintaining androgen-dependent functions. NES/testosterone gel has completed phase 2b evaluation in couples; approval remains outstanding. Proposed completion test: FDA approval after a pivotal couples study with at least 500 couple-years of contraceptive exposure, a pregnancy rate below 2 per 100 couple-years, acceptable safety, and documented recovery of sperm production and fertility after cessation. Test set by: FDA would decide approval; WHO's September 2026 male-contraceptive TPP establishes efficacy, safety and reversibility as development criteria. The exposure minimum and pregnancy-rate threshold here are editorial proposals. Sources given: [WHO male contraceptive target product profiles](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240124950) ; [NICHD 2025 contraceptive development report](https://annualreport.nichd.nih.gov/blithe.html) ; [Developer's current clinical pipeline](https://www.contraline.com/trials).

page.title: Reversible hormonal male contraception
page.definition: An approved hormonal drug taken by a man prevents pregnancy by suppressing sperm production. Treatment lowers testosterone production inside the testes, where sperm production requires high concentrations, while supplying enough testosterone-like activity elsewhere in the body to maintain sexual function. Sperm production recovers after treatment stops. A daily gel containing segesterone acetate and testosterone has reached couples trials and remains investigational.

goal.need: In a survey across six African and Asian countries, about one-third of respondents who had used male contraceptives were dissatisfied with them. Condoms and withdrawal require action during sex. Vasectomy is intended to be permanent. A reversible drug would let men take responsibility for pregnancy prevention between sexual encounters. Once sperm suppression is confirmed, a partner who has intolerable side effects from her contraceptive could stop using it. Condoms would still be needed for protection against sexually transmitted infections.

completion.title: FDA approves a hormonal male contraceptive for reversible pregnancy prevention.
completion.criterion: FDA issues an approval letter for a new drug application for reversible hormonal male contraception. The product meets statutory standards for safety, effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling. Adequate clinical evidence supports its intended contraceptive use and claimed reversibility under the approved conditions of use.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.105(c) and 314.125(b).
completion.threshold_quote: FDA will approve an NDA after it determines that the drug meets the statutory standards for safety and effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling,
completion.basis: NICHD explicitly seeks FDA approval. The approval decision evaluates the intended use and the complete evidence package. WHO's target profiles guide development and regulatory review. Contraline identifies NES/T gel as investigational and unapproved.

milestones.title: Preclinical studies support human testing of a hormonal male contraceptive.
milestones.criterion: Animal or in vitro pharmacology and toxicology support the sponsor's conclusion that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe. For each nonclinical study subject to Good Laboratory Practice regulations, the application states whether the study complied and explains any noncompliance.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), governing the preclinical evidence supporting an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: Phase 1 establishes human pharmacokinetics and tolerability of a hormonal male contraceptive.
milestones.criterion: Human studies characterize the drug's pharmacokinetics, pharmacological effects and side effects with increasing doses in enough detail to design well-controlled, scientifically valid phase 2 studies.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1), defining the information required from phase 1 investigations.
milestones.threshold_quote: sufficient information about the drug's pharmacokinetics and pharmacological effects should be obtained to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: A hormonal male contraceptive suppresses sperm concentration to ≤1 million/mL.
milestones.criterion: In a six-month study, measure the proportion of men whose sperm concentration falls to ≤1 million/mL. In a couples efficacy trial, confirm that the male partner has reached this threshold before the couple relies on the regimen alone.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendations 43 and 45.
milestones.threshold_quote: suppression of spermatogenesis (sperm concentration ≤1 million/mL) in a 6-month study.

milestones.title: Over 95% of men regain the adult sperm concentration range within 6 months of stopping hormonal contraception.
milestones.criterion: In phase IIb and III studies, follow all men for recovery of sperm concentration after treatment stops. Assess return to the adult male reference range over six months, with a proposed recovery goal of over 95%. Time to recovery depends on the formulation and its duration of action. Sperm concentration is a surrogate for fertility.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, section 10.4, proposed regulatory recommendations.
milestones.threshold_quote: recovery after hormonal male contraception should be over 95%.

milestones.title: Couples trials estimate one-year pregnancy probability with 5,000 men-months of sole-method use.
milestones.criterion: For one regimen, accrue the proposed 5,000 men-months of exposure while couples rely on it alone. Use partner pregnancies to estimate cumulative pregnancy probability over 365 days of use by the Kaplan–Meier method and report its 95% confidence interval.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 46 and the proposed exposure target in section 10.4.
milestones.threshold_quote: 5000 men-months of exposure would be sufficient to demonstrate efficacy.

milestones.title: A hormonal male contraceptive has safety exposure in about 1,500 men, including 100 treated for one year.
milestones.criterion: For one product, the general ICH safety database includes about 1,500 exposed individuals. Usually 300–600 receive intended clinical doses for six months and 100 receive them for at least one year. The andrology societies recommend at least 300 men for six months and at least 100 for one year. ICH allows for larger databases for some preventive treatments given to healthy people.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, E1A guideline adopted by FDA; applied to male contraception in EAA–ASA recommendation 44.
milestones.threshold_quote: 100 patients exposed for a minimum of one-year is considered to be acceptable to include as part of the safety data base.

milestones.title: Animal studies demonstrate that the hormonal candidate suppresses sperm production.
milestones.criterion: Describe the candidate's hormonal mechanism and demonstrate its effect on sperm production in treated animals by sperm counts or examination of testicular tissue.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8)(i), for the animal pharmacology evidence in an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: A section describing the pharmacological effects and mechanism(s) of action of the drug in animals

milestones.title: A dose-finding study measures the proportion of men with both LH and FSH ≤1.0 IU/L at day 28.
milestones.criterion: After 28 days of treatment, report the percentage of men whose serum luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) are each ≤1.0 international unit per litre, with a 95% confidence interval for that percentage.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 43 and section 10.4.
milestones.threshold_quote: both FSH and LH suppressed to ≤1.0 IU/L after 4 weeks (day 28) of treatment.

milestones.title: FDA accepts a new drug application for reversible hormonal male contraception for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA files a new drug application for the proposed contraceptive indication after determining that it is sufficiently complete for substantive review and notifies the applicant in writing. FDA ordinarily makes the filing determination within 60 days of receipt.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1)–(2).
milestones.threshold_quote: The filing of an NDA means that FDA has made a threshold determination that the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

results.finding: Testicular histology showed hypospermatogenesis in 3 of 3 cynomolgus macaques examined after repeat DMAU injections.
results.quote: Moreover, microscopic evaluation of the testes, as shown in Figure  7 , showed moderate diffuse seminiferous tubular hypospermatogenesis on Day 30 in all three NHPs given five IM injections of 30 mg/kg DMAU but not in any of the three control animals.

results.finding: Repeat-dose DMAU studies in cynomolgus macaques (6–7 per oral group, 3–6 per injection group) found zero toxicologically significant drug-related findings.
results.detail: The paper identifies both repeat-dose toxicity studies as compliant with 21 CFR Part 58. Application-level disclosure for every applicable nonclinical study remains unverified.
results.quote: Repeat dose oral and IM administrations were well‐tolerated with no significant toxicological findings.

results.finding: In a phase 1b trial of oral DMAU with 100 treated men, peak serum drug concentrations occurred 4–6 hours after dosing.
results.detail: Serial sampling on days 1 and 28 showed no statistically significant change in pharmacokinetic parameters with repeat dosing for either formulation.
results.quote: Following oral administration of DMAU with food, peak serum concentrations of DMAU and DMA were achieved 4 to 6 hours later for both formulations

results.finding: At day 28, 92% of 13 men taking 400 mg DMAU in castor oil had both LH and FSH below 1.0 IU/L.
results.quote: All subjects in the P400 group and 12 of 13 subjects (92%) in the C400 group achieved suppression of LH and FSH (to <1 IU/L).

results.finding: After 28 days of oral DMAU, 4 of 59 men had sperm concentrations below 5 million/mL.
results.quote: Interestingly, 4 of 59 men in the treatment groups did achieve sperm concentrations of <5 million/mL at 28 days, whereas none did in the placebo group.

results.finding: The oral DMAU safety analysis included 73 men exposed to active drug in a 28-day trial.
results.quote: The most common adverse event overall was headache, reported by 13 subjects [5 of 27 (19%) placebo, 8 of 73 (11%) drug].

results.finding: Among 320 men given the injectable combination, an estimated 95.9% of continuing users reached ≤1 million sperm/mL by week 24.
results.quote:
Of the 320 participants, 95.9 of 100 continuing users (95% confidence interval [CI], 92.8 –
97.9) suppressed to a sperm concentration less than or equal to 1 million/mL within 24 weeks
(Kaplan-Meier method).

results.finding: Among 266 couples relying on the injectable combination, cumulative pregnancy probability was estimated at 1.57%.
results.detail: All pregnancies occurred before week 16. Injections ended early, and fewer couples completed the efficacy phase than planned.
results.quote:
During the efficacy phase of up to 56 weeks, 4 pregnancies occurred
among the partners of the 266 male participants, with the rate of 1.57 per 100 continuing users
(95% CI, 0.59 – 4.14).

results.finding: Among 247 men analyzed for recovery after the injectable combination, an estimated 94.8% reached the study’s reference threshold by recovery week 52.
results.detail: Seventeen men who left during efficacy had no recovery follow-up. Two additional men were excluded from the recovery analysis because semen results were missing.
results.quote:
The cumulative reversibility of suppression of spermatogenesis after 52 weeks
of recovery was 94.8 per 100 continuing users (95% CI, 91.5–97.1).

results.finding: The injectable combination’s phase II safety cohort included 320 men who received at least one injection.
results.detail: The total counts men after a single injection, so it does not establish that at least 300 men received intended doses for six months or that at least 100 received them for one year.

results.finding: Among 1,549 men pooled across androgen-only and combination regimens, the estimated six-month sperm concentration recovery probability was 67%.
results.detail: The sample size and recovery estimate apply to both regimen cases pooled. Shorter-acting testosterone preparations were associated with faster recovery.
results.quote: The typical probability of recovery to 20 million per mL was 67% (61-72) within 6 months, 90% (85-93) within 12 months, 96% (92-98) within 16 months, and 100% within 24 months.

results.finding: Among 15 healthy men evaluated at day 28 on 400 mg/day of oral 11β-MNTDC alone, 66.7% had both serum LH and FSH ≤1.0 IU/L.
results.detail: The 400 mg arm had 16 treated participants, and the reported day-28 percentage uses a denominator of 15.
results.quote: Overall (including data from all time points), none of the participants in the placebo group, 46.7% (7/15) participants in the 200-mg group and 66.7% (10/15) of the participants in the 400-mg group had gonadotropins suppressed to ≤ 1.0 IU/L at day 28

case_label = "Regimen". Reason: The number of active drugs distinguishes the treatment groups in comparative trials even when both groups use the same route of administration.

definition = "An approved hormonal drug taken by a man prevents pregnancy by suppressing sperm production. Treatment lowers testosterone production inside the testes, where sperm production requires high concentrations, while supplying enough testosterone-like activity elsewhere in the body to maintain sexual function. Sperm production recovers after treatment stops. A daily gel containing segesterone acetate and testosterone has reached couples trials and remains investigational.". Reason: The current definition leaves unexplained how the same treatment can suppress sperm production and preserve sexual function.

goal.need = "In a survey across six African and Asian countries, about one-third of respondents who had used male contraceptives were dissatisfied with them. Condoms and withdrawal require action during sex. Vasectomy is intended to be permanent. A reversible drug would let men take responsibility for pregnancy prevention between sexual encounters. Once sperm suppression is confirmed, a partner who has intolerable side effects from her contraceptive could stop using it. Condoms would still be needed for protection against sexually transmitted infections.". Reason: The six-country survey measures dissatisfaction with men's existing options directly, and the revision explains which couples could benefit and when they could rely on the drug.

add statement by Participants in the 10th Summit Meeting on Male Contraception, 2007: "hormonal contraceptive products for men should now be proposed for development for general use.". Reason: The summit consensus explicitly names hormonal contraception for general use as the goal, which the two existing statements describe in broader terms.

add not found: "No regulator or professional society statement opposing development of reversible hormonal male contraception as a class was found.". Reason: Published objections to particular regimens do not answer whether an expert body disputes the overall goal.
add case "Single agent". Reason: Testosterone alone and single molecules with both androgen and progestin activity have been studied as single-agent contraceptives.
add case "Combination regimen". Reason: Adding a second active drug changed sperm suppression in a randomized trial, so combination results need their own case.
reorder to ['m1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm5', 'm4', 'm6']. Reason: The couples trial measures pregnancy during sole-method use before participants stop treatment for recovery follow-up.
